question: Which element of Group 13 of the periodic table liquefies just above room temperature?
solution:
The correct option is __**Gallium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Group 13 elements are also known as **Boron Family.**
 
• The **elements are Boron, Aluminium, Gallium, Indium, Thallium.**
 
• The general** electronic configuration** for the group 13 elements is ns2 np1.
 
• Gallium was discovered in 1875 by French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran.
 
• Atomic number of **Gallium** is 31 and chemical symbol is **Ga.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boron** is the lightest element of Boron family, the chemical symbol **B** and atomic number is 5. In its crystalline form it is a brittle, dark, lustrous metalloid; in its amorphus form it is a brown powder.
 
• **Aluminium's** chemical symbol **Al** and atomic number 13. It has a density lower than those of other common metals.
 
• **Thallium **is a chemical element with the symbol **Tl** and atomic number 81. It is a gray post-transition metal that is not found free in nature.
 
• **Indium** is a chemical element with the symbol **In** and atomic number 49. Indium is the softest metal that is not an alkali metal. It is a silvery-white metal that resembles Tin in appearance. It is a post-transition metal that makes up 0.21 parts per million of the Earth's crust.
